item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: four angles varied in size and labeled P, Q, R, and S from left to right.]

In which of the following are the angles ordered by size, from least to greatest?
item.figure_description:
Four angles are shown side by side, labeled from left to right as P, Q, R, and S. Each angle has a horizontal ray pointing to the right, a second ray extending from the left endpoint, and a curved arc indicating the angle between the two rays:
- Angle P is an acute angle opening upward and to the right at approximately 45°.
- Angle Q is an obtuse angle opening upward and to the left at approximately 120°.
- Angle R is a right angle (90°) formed with a vertical ray extending straight up.
- Angle S is an acute angle opening upward and to the right at approximately 30°, smaller than angle P.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: One of these angles is a right angle. Which one?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four angles labeled A, B, C, and D:
- Option A shows two connected line segments meeting at an apex pointing upward, one segment sloping down to the left at roughly 45° and the other sloping down to the right at roughly 45°.
- Option B shows two connected line segments meeting at a bottom vertex, one extending nearly vertically upward and the other slanting upward and to the right, forming an angle of approximately 25°.
- Option C shows two connected line segments meeting at a top vertex, one extending vertically downward and the other slanting downward and to the left, forming an angle of approximately 20°.
- Option D shows two connected line segments meeting at a bottom vertex, one slanting downward to the right and the other extending horizontally to the right, forming an angle of approximately 120°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Figures that are the same size and shape are called congruent figures.

[Image: Four figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4]

Which two figures are congruent?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectilinear figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4:
- Figure 1: An L-shaped polygon with a horizontal top arm extending to the right and a vertical arm on the left extending downwards.
- Figure 2: A large rectangular/square shape with a small rectangular tab extending out to the upper right.
- Figure 3: An L-shaped polygon with a tall vertical left arm and a shorter horizontal bottom arm extending to the right.
- Figure 4: An L-shaped polygon with a horizontal bottom arm extending to the left and a vertical arm on the right extending upwards, having the same arm lengths and thickness as Figure 1 rotated 180 degrees.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A shaded geometric shape]

The shape above is rotated by 90° clockwise. Which shape is the result?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, a shaded grey shape formed by two perpendicular arms meeting at a top-left corner: a longer vertical arm extending downwards and a shorter horizontal arm extending to the right. A small vertical oval cutout/hole is positioned near the right end of the top horizontal arm.

Below are four multiple-choice options:
- Option A: A shaded grey shape with a corner at the bottom-left; a long vertical arm extends upwards and a shorter horizontal arm extends to the right along the bottom. A vertical oval hole is near the right end of the bottom horizontal arm.
- Option B: A shaded grey shape with a corner at the top-right; a shorter horizontal arm extends to the left along the top and a longer vertical arm extends downwards on the right. A vertical oval hole is near the left end of the top horizontal arm.
- Option C: A shaded grey shape with a corner at the top-right; a longer horizontal arm extends to the left along the top and a shorter vertical arm extends downwards on the right. A horizontal oval hole is near the bottom end of the vertical arm.
- Option D: A shaded grey shape with a corner at the bottom-right; a shorter horizontal arm extends to the left along the bottom and a longer vertical arm extends upwards on the right. A vertical oval hole is near the left end of the bottom horizontal arm.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
